correctness.rationale: The exact terminal observable is F(u)=Phi(u_d), gradient phi(u_d)e_d, and E phi(U_d)^2=1/(2pi sqrt3). The centered indicator coefficient is always plus/minus 1/2, so each inner score belongs to the fixed Gaussian endpoint span, has nonzero value a.s. because the d-by-ell endpoint matrix has full column rank, and hence every positive-eigenvalue matrix eigenvector lies in that span. Haar-uniform ell-planes have projection energy Beta(ell/2,(d-ell)/2). Gaussian regression gives E[Phi(U_d)|v^TU]=Phi(cY/sqrt(2-c²)); a bivariate normal orthant identity yields Var=arcsin(c²/2)/(2pi). Monotonicity makes projected e_d the optimal direction; convex arcsine lies below its endpoint chord, proving linear lower bound. For ell=1 outer products equal ZZ^T/4 algebraically. Independent 3 reused-endpoint identity cases and 21 exact risk-floor checks passed. The theorem is explicitly restricted to fresh Gaussian prediction inputs.
residual_risks: The tests are finite and do not replace the all-parameter proof.
